title: Design a Meeting Scheduler / Calendar
relevance: High — staple LLD / OOD whiteboard (and occasional machine-coding) question; Amazon, Microsoft, Google/Meta-style loops, Qualcomm, Atlassian, and Indian product cos use it to probe interval conflict detection, room allocation Strategy, Observer notifications, recurrence, and the double-booking race.
company_notes: Campus / machine-coding (Flipkart, Uber, Swiggy, Amazon new-grad, Indian product cos): meeting-room booking CLI where working conflict-free book/cancel + capacity beats unfinished recurrence. Experienced LLD (FAANG / Microsoft / Atlassian / Qualcomm-style): same domain with deeper probes — per-room concurrency, Strategy vs switch, Observer notifications, find-common-slot, recurrence parent/instance, tentative holds. Among the top ~15 canonical LLD problems; template for interval-resource booking.

phases.goal: Clarify interview flavor and lock FR/NFR before inventing scope.

must_hit.point: State which flavor is in scope: (A) meeting-room booking with scarce rooms and no double-book, and/or (B) personal calendar with per-user calendars, invites, recurrence, and find mutual free time.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate asks rooms-only vs people calendars vs both, then names the shared Interval/conflict logic either flavor needs.

must_hit.point: List typical room-scheduler FRs: list rooms; book [start, end) if free and capacity covers attendees; cancel/release; list free rooms; notify participants; meeting history.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They walk a FR checklist covering capacity, booking rules, participants, and notifications before coding.

must_hit.point: List typical calendar FRs: create/update/cancel events; invite + RSVP (ACCEPT/DECLINE/TENTATIVE); conflict checks; optional recurring series; find earliest common slot.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They distinguish organizer/participant flows: schedule/invite/RSVP/cancel/calendar-update.

must_hit.point: State NFRs: no double-booking under concurrent requests; OCP for assignment/notify/recurrence; modular packages; demonstrable main/CLI.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They call out concurrency safety and extensibility as first-class, not afterthoughts.

probes: Are we designing room booking, personal calendars, or both — and do we need RSVP, recurrence, find-common-slot, timezones, and concurrency?

hints.1: Ask what scarce resource you are protecting first.
hints.2: Separate room-scheduler FRs from calendar FRs, then share conflict assumptions.
hints.3: Rooms + people? capacity? RSVP? recurrence? mutual free time? multi-TZ? concurrent book?

phases.goal: Name core entities and the conflict/overlap rules they own.

must_hit.point: Name core entities: User (organizer/participant), Calendar (per user and/or per room), Meeting/Event, MeetingRoom (id, capacity, amenities), Interval/TimeSlot (start, end), optional RecurrenceRule, Notification, MeetingScheduler facade.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Whiteboard lists these types with Calendar attached to users and/or rooms.

must_hit.point: Treat Calendar as a conflict detector: primary ops isAvailable(interval) / getConflicts(interval), not a dumb meeting dump; prefer sorted intervals or an interval tree; give each user and each room its own calendar.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They say Calendar answers free/busy and mutates bookings, not MeetingScheduler scanning a global list.

must_hit.point: State the overlap rule: intervals A and B conflict iff A.start < B.end && B.start < A.end; prefer half-open [start, end) so touching edges are not conflicts.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They write the predicate and note adjacent end==next-start is allowed under half-open.

must_hit.point: Model booking lifecycle states when probed: TENTATIVE (short hold) → CONFIRMED → CANCELLED / EXPIRED rather than only booked/free.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They mention holds before confirm when the interviewer asks about tentative booking.

probes: What objects own capacity, free/busy, and RSVP — and when do two intervals conflict?

hints.1: Start from people, rooms, time ranges, and the thing that detects conflicts.
hints.2: Give User and MeetingRoom each a Calendar; Meeting holds Interval plus RSVP map.
hints.3: Conflict iff A.start < B.end && B.start < A.end; use half-open [start, end).

phases.goal: Sketch facade, calendars, strategies, and observers with clear responsibilities.

must_hit.point: MeetingScheduler is a Facade orchestrating schedule/cancel/respond/getAvailableRooms/findEarliestSlot over rooms, users, meetings maps and a RoomAssignmentStrategy — no overlap math inlined if Calendar owns it.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Class diagram shows Scheduler calling calendars/strategy/observers, not embedding interval scans.

must_hit.point: RoomAssignmentStrategy interface (e.g. FirstAvailable / MinCapacityFit) picks a room; RecurrenceRule (+ Factory from DAILY/WEEKLY/MONTHLY) is optional Strategy for occurrencesIn(window).
must_hit.evidence_hint: They draw Strategy interfaces instead of switch/if for room pick and recurrence expand.

must_hit.point: Meeting notifies Observers (NotificationService / User) on CREATED|UPDATED|CANCELLED|REMINDER; Singleton scheduler is optional for demos — prefer DI in production.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They name Observer for invites and caveat Singleton vs constructor injection.

must_hit.point: Name key APIs: addRoom; bookMeeting(organizer, participants, interval, minCapacity?) → Meeting|Conflict; cancelMeeting; respondToInvite; getAvailableRooms; findEarliestSlot; optional reschedule/getHistory.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They list these methods on the facade before coding.

probes: Walk the class diagram: who owns conflict checks, who picks the room, who sends notifications?

hints.1: Facade + Calendar + Strategy + Observer is the expected pattern set.
hints.3: Sketch MeetingScheduler, User+Calendar, MeetingRoom+Calendar, Meeting, Interval, RoomAssignmentStrategy, RecurrenceRule, Notification.

phases.goal: Implement conflict-free book/cancel and stretch algorithms without inventing scope.

must_hit.point: bookMeeting filters by capacity then assignment strategy, checks room (and people if in scope) calendars for conflicts, inserts booking, then notifies — cancel frees the room calendar and notifies.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Happy-path walk: capacity → pick room → isAvailable → add → notify; cancel reverses.

must_hit.point: Find earliest common slot: union busy intervals across attendees in the window, merge overlaps, walk gaps, take first gap that fits the requested duration.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They describe merge-busy-then-walk-gaps, not brute nested loops over every minute without a plan.

must_hit.point: Prefer sorted free/busy structures so conflict check is not a full O(n) scan of history; for machine coding, in-memory sorted lists are fine at tens–hundreds of rooms with meetings/day per room in the dozens.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They justify sorted list/interval tree and keep domain logic out of the CLI driver.

must_hit.point: Store times as UTC instants internally; display in user TZ; expand recurrence in one IANA zone when multi-TZ is in scope.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They say UTC storage + organizer IANA zone for RRULE expand, matching the Google-style model.

probes: How do you book without double-booking, and how would you find the earliest mutual free slot?

hints.1: Implement room book/cancel + conflict detection before recurrence polish.
hints.2: Capacity filter, then Strategy pick, then Calendar check+insert, then Observer notify.
hints.3: Common slot = merge attendee busy unions in window, walk gaps for first fit ≥ duration.

phases.goal: Show OCP via Strategy/Observer/Factory and lazy recurrence rather than god-classes.

must_hit.point: New room-pick policies (FCFS, min-capacity-fit, nearest) swap RoomAssignmentStrategy without editing the facade; hardcoded first-free passes demos but Strategy is the expected answer.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They point at the Strategy interface when asked to prefer smallest fitting room or a floor preference.

must_hit.point: Add Slack + email by new Observer/notifier channels — do not branch if (channel == …) inside Meeting; Calendar owns conflicts, Strategy owns pick, Observer owns notify, Scheduler orchestrates (SRP/OCP).
must_hit.evidence_hint: They refuse to grow Meeting into a god-class holding reminders, channels, and room search.

must_hit.point: Recurrence: store a rule (+ optional exceptions); expand only inside the query/book window — do not materialize years up front; declining/editing one instance uses exception/EXDATE, not mutating the whole RRULE (parent + instances).
must_hit.evidence_hint: They cite rule + lazy windowed expand and instance exceptions, optionally naming RFC 5545 RRULE/RDATE/EXDATE.

probes: How would you add a new room-assignment policy or notification channel without rewriting MeetingScheduler?

hints.1: Ask what should change by adding a class versus editing a switch.
hints.2: Strategy for pick/recurrence expand; Observer for notify; Factory for rule creation.
hints.3: Lazy RRULE expand in window + EXDATE for one declined occurrence; new notifier implements Observer.

phases.goal: Protect the no-overlap invariant under concurrent book/accept without over-serializing.

must_hit.point: Invariant: no two ACTIVE bookings for a room overlap; check-then-act is a race — make check-free + insert one critical section under a per-room lock (or optimistic version / DB exclusion constraint).
must_hit.evidence_hint: They show synchronized/locked book path or version conflict when two organizers book the same room for overlapping times.

must_hit.point: Per-user calendar locks for invite accept that must block conflicts; ConcurrentHashMap catalogs alone are not an atomic book — still lock per room/calendar on check+insert.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They separate safe maps from the book critical section and mention personal-calendar locking for ACCEPT.

must_hit.point: Coarse global lock is correct but over-serializes unrelated rooms; do not hold the lock while sending emails — notify async / after commit.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They choose per-room granularity and move notification outside the critical section.

probes: Two organizers book Room A for overlapping times at once — how do you prevent double-booking?

hints.1: Correct overlap math is not enough under concurrency.
hints.2: Atomic check+insert; prefer per-room lock over one global lock.
hints.3: Lock room calendar for isAvailable+add; unlock before Observer notify; optimistic version is an alternative.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Room-only ships faster for machine coding; composing per-user calendars behind the same Calendar abstraction unlocks RSVP conflict checks and find-common-slot without duplicating overlap logic.

tradeoffs.topic: Strategy vs hardcoded first free room
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Hardcoded first-free passes demos; Strategy is the expected answer when product rules prefer smallest fit, nearest room, or floor constraints without editing the facade.
Correct overlap code still double-books under concurrency unless check+insert is one critical section (per-room lock) or DB/optimistic version enforces the no-overlap invariant.

Materializing simplifies conflict checks but explodes storage; lazy expand inside the query/book window plus exceptions (EXDATE / overridden instances) is the production answer (RFC 5545 / Google parent+instances).
Singleton is fine for demos; prefer constructor injection for tests — same caveat as parking lot / Splitwise.

gotchas.trap: Two organizers book Room A 10:00–11:00 at once and both succeed.
gotchas.correction: Classic check-then-act race; synchronize the book path with per-room lock or optimistic version so check-free + insert is atomic.

gotchas.trap: Meeting ends at 11:00 and next starts at 11:00 treated as conflict.
gotchas.correction: Use half-open [start, end) so adjacent slots are allowed.

gotchas.trap: 10 people with rooms of capacity 6 and 12 — wrong room chosen or capacity ignored.
gotchas.correction: Capacity-filter before assignment; MinCapacityFit (or smallest-fit) as Strategy encodes the product rule.

gotchas.trap: Decline one occurrence of a weekly standup by editing the whole series rule.
gotchas.correction: Add an exception on that instance (EXDATE / overridden instance); do not mutate the whole RRULE.

gotchas.trap: Find a 30-min slot for Alice, Bob, Carol this week with ad-hoc nested loops and no merge plan.
gotchas.correction: Union/merge busy intervals across attendees in the window, then walk gaps for the first fit.

gotchas.trap: Add Slack + email by if-channel branches inside Meeting.
gotchas.correction: New Observer/notifier implementations; keep Meeting free of channel switches.

gotchas.trap: Timezone/DST bugs from storing local wall times or expanding recurrence across mixed zones casually.
gotchas.correction: Store UTC instants; expand recurrence in organizer IANA TZ (Google model).

gotchas.trap: God-class Meeting holding recurrence strings, reminder prefs, and room search.
gotchas.correction: Split SRP: Calendar conflicts, Strategy pick, Observer notify, Scheduler orchestration.

gotchas.trap: Finishing recurrence UML but failing mandatory book/cancel without double-booking.
gotchas.correction: Mandatory first: conflict-free book/cancel + capacity; recurrence is stretch.
